Stated Claim / Post Context:
Islamabad Prepares for PTI Protest as Road Barriers Remain

Islamabad maintains road barriers and security measures ahead of a postponed PTI protest march demanding Imran Khan's release on October 4.

Actual Article Body:
Journos News graphic showing security restrictions, reopened routes and key dates surrounding the postponement of PTI's Islamabad protest march to October 4. - Journos News, File.

ISLAMABAD, Pakistan – Shipping containers and other barriers remain deployed along key roads in and around Pakistan’s capital as authorities prepare for a protest march by supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, despite the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf having postponed the demonstration by a week.

The PTI originally planned to march on Islamabad on September 27 to demand Khan’s release. The party later moved the date to October 4, while authorities began removing some of the barriers from major highways connecting Islamabad with the northwest. Several restrictions inside and around the capital, however, have remained.
